commit.message:
fix(app): judge a turned path's axial rapids in the meridian plane against the revolved stock

The column cannot see the meridian (#96), so the turned family's axial
rapids were exempt and unwatched. They are now judged in the turning
plane: the nose disc against the part and the setup stock revolved
about the fitted axis, less this path's earlier feeds and the stock the
program ahead faced. A conviction is RapidInStock and blocks the post.

Partial: the lathe_post goldens (box stock wider than the bar) now
convict; fixture vs kernel decision held.

Refs #103

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(app): lathe fixtures stand in bar-sized stock; blades and gauges judged at their tip

The meridian rapid law convicted the lathe suites' approaches into a
40 mm box stock round 12-20 mm bars - real against the declared box,
since the turning kernels never cut stock beyond the part (#130). The
fixtures now declare a cylinder of the bar's own size; no NC golden
changed. Only Turning and Bore inserts are judged by their nose disc:
a blade, thread or form gauge's moves carry the tip (a form's
nose_radius is its crown arc, which convicted every clean form
traverse).

Held: turning_bore's three tests - the law reads the bore of the part
and of the stock as solid, so a boring approach is always convicted.

Refs #103

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(app): the meridian rapid law reads the bore as air and credits a pilot drill ahead

The part and the stock are read per station as an annulus between the
hole and the skin (ray parity from the axis), so a boring bar's approach
down a bored part or a tube is judged against what is really there. An
axial Drill ahead in the setup is credited as its cylinder and point
cone, on a lathe too (the facing-only prior is unchanged). The
turning_bore fixtures drill their pilot first; a boring approach into a
solid bar with no pilot is still convicted and blocks the post.

Fixes #103

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(app): the meridian rapid law judges a boring bar's body and a blade's band

Review of PR #135. A Bore tool's body (its radius about the nose, up its
flute and shank) must fit the hole a pilot drilled, not the nose alone:
a 10 mm bar down a 4 mm pilot is convicted, and the turning_bore pilot
is an 11 mm drill. Groove, part and form blades are judged across their
band (the move is the band's centre), a thread across its crest. Arc
feeds credit nothing (a chord is not the sweep), and a drill with no
stated point is read as 118 degrees, not flat.

Fixes #103

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(app,motion): a boring bar's body lies toward the axis and the bar rapids centred in the hole

Re-review of PR #135 (B3). The insert sits at the bar's edge, so the
rapid law reads a Bore body as signed radius [rho - d, rho] - a bar with
its nose on the axis reaches a whole diameter off it - not centred on
the nose. The bore kernel now approaches and retracts with the bar and
its nose centred on the spindle (nose at bar_radius - nose/2 on the
cutting side), so a pilot just over the bar's size admits it: the
turning_bore fixture's 11 mm pilot under its 12 mm bore passes honestly,
and a 10 mm bar with its nose on the axis in that pilot is convicted.

Fixes #103

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(app,motion): a boring bar's head and shank are judged apart, the kernel centres the whole bar

Re-review of PR #135 (B4). A shank wider than the head reaches past the
nose. The rapid law now reads the head [-head_d, 0] over the flute and
the shank as the union of its edge-aligned and coaxial readings over
the shank length (motion::turning::bar_spans, shared with the kernel),
and the bore kernel centres the whole bar on the spindle
(centred_nose). A stepped bar too wide for its pilot is convicted on its
shank; at the app level the body is pinned at its full size.

Fixes #103

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(app,motion): the lathe facing approach feeds in, and the meridian re-reads the column's radial convictions

After merging #106, facing.nc gained convictions on the inward rapid at
each face depth: real - the kernel rapided to the model's reach through
stock wider than the model, below the previous pass's floor. The facing
kernel now feeds that move in (rapids stay outside the work), and its
fixture stands in bar-sized stock. The outward retracts the column
convicted (main's 11/15/19, turning_bore's off-wall rapid, a chamfer's
retract) are false: the footprint disc about the nose is a mill's
reading. For the turned family the meridian law now re-reads an in-plane
radial rapid the column convicted (it may acquit, it adds nothing), a
blade's feed kerf spans its band, and the turning_bore pilot is 11.2 mm.

Fixes #103

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(app): the meridian law owns every rapid of a turning op, the column's footprint none

Main went red after PR #138 (#159): the footprint rapid law read the
lathe's radial rapids as a mill disc about the nose and convicted
turning_bore's off-wall retract, a chamfer's retract and facing's
own-kerf retracts - all false in the turning plane. For the turned
family the meridian law now judges every in-plane rapid, axial and
radial, and the column's word on them is dropped. It credits the
turning ops ahead, a thread's helix as constant radius, and a blade's
band or a thread's V outward of its tip. The real convictions it finds
stand: a taper ride alone on the 20 mm bar retracts through the ring it
leaves (pinned; the clean rides stand on a pre-turned blank), and the
profile golden's finish, posted ahead of its rough, retracts through
uncut stock (one recorded WARN line, program text unchanged).

Fixes #103
Fixes #159

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(app): an earlier op's kerf keeps its own reach, and the profile golden posts rough before finish

Fifth review of PR #135. The blade-band widening of a kerf applies only
to this op's own cuts - a groove's band no longer credits material under
an earlier face cut (pinned). The profile golden's finish is renamed so
the rough posts first (the golden diff is the two sections swapped and
the WARN line gone); finish ahead of rough is pinned as convicted by
name. Doc notes on the helix-credit approximation and the OD blade side.

Fixes #103
Fixes #159
